about: Example expressions as FB2 weight sets, and a short talking sequence as META visemes; examples/make_expression_frames.py turns them into frames.

Illustrative input for the face examples, not RCEF mapping data: nothing in profiles/ or mappings/ reads this file, and no golden comes from it. It is JSON because msf-tools reads every TOML file in the repository as pack authoring.

sources.EMF: Wikipedia, 'Facial Action Coding System', revision 1357638399 (2026-06-03), raw wikitext lines 36-53: emotion table (EMFACS), citing Friesen & Ekman, EMFACS-7 (1983, unpublished)
sources.DU: Du, Tao & Martinez, 'Compound facial expressions of emotion', PNAS 111(15) 2014, doi:10.1073/pnas.1322355111, Table 1 (prototypical AUs, variants in brackets)
sources.AU: Wikipedia, 'Facial Action Coding System', revision 1357638399, raw wikitext lines 87-264: action units (AU number and name)
sources.VIS: OpenXR XR_META_face_tracking_visemes: viseme table with example words (lines 130-250) and the sum-to-one rule (lines 104-107)

intensity_note: FACS intensity letters as FB2 weights. ASSUMPTION: neither FACS nor FB2 defines a numeric scale, so A-E are taken as linear steps, and a prototype AU with no stated intensity is taken as C. The optional variants in DU are left out.
au_channels_note: AU -> FB2 channel. FB2 channel names are the FACS action-unit names (AU); the FB2 specification gives no AU numbers, so this is a name correspondence. A bilateral AU sets every side of the channel equally; "L12" or "R12" sets one side. AU 30 has a direction instead of a side. AU 17 (chin raiser) maps to CHIN_RAISER_B only: FB2 describes CHIN_RAISER_T as the upper-lip motion the chin raiser induces, so the top channel is not set separately.
no_fb2_channel_note: AUs in a prototype that FB2 has no channel for; frames that need them say so.
expressions_note: 18 expressions, then gaze one direction at a time (FB2 opposing gaze directions are exclusive).

expressions.name: anger
assumptions: AU 24 comes from [DU] and is added to the [EMF] set.

expressions.name: disgust
assumptions: The union of the two sources: AU 10 from [DU], AU 15 from [EMF].

expressions.name: contempt
assumptions: Single source: [DU] has no contempt prototype.

expressions.name: happily surprised
assumptions: Single source: [EMF] has no compound expressions.

expressions.name: brow raise
sources: AU: 1 inner brow raiser, 2 outer brow raiser
assumptions: Weight 0.8 is chosen for display; no source gives an intensity.

expressions.name: squint
assumptions: Weights 0.7 and 0.3 are chosen for display; no source gives intensities.

expressions.name: wink left
assumptions: A wink is taken as one closed eye with a slight cheek raise (0.3, chosen for display).

expressions.name: wink right
assumptions: A wink is taken as one closed eye with a slight cheek raise (0.3, chosen for display).

expressions.name: smirk left
sources: AU: 12 lip corner puller, one side

expressions.name: pucker
assumptions: Weights 0.8 and 0.3 are chosen for display; no source gives intensities.

expressions.name: cheek puff
sources: AU: 34 cheek puff, 8 lips toward each other
assumptions: The lips are taken as sealed while the cheeks puff (AU 8 at 0.5); weights chosen for display.

expressions.name: lip suck
assumptions: Weight 0.7 is chosen for display; no source gives an intensity.

expressions.name: look left
assumptions: Weight 0.8 is chosen for display; no source gives an intensity.

expressions.name: look right
assumptions: Weight 0.8 is chosen for display; no source gives an intensity.

expressions.name: look up
assumptions: Weight 0.8 is chosen for display; no source gives an intensity.

expressions.name: look down
assumptions: Weight 0.8 is chosen for display; no source gives an intensity.

talk.note: "bed car toe book", the specification's own example words (VIS), one viseme per sound, starting and ending in silence.
sources: VIS: example words bed (PP, E, DD), car (KK, AA, RR), toe (DD, OH), book (PP, OU, KK)
